findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
findings.comment: The plumbing line under the triple sink in the back is still observed to be leaking. Discussed with PIC, a new triple sink has been ordered. Inspectors observed delivery on sink will take 2-3 weeks. A follow up is scheduled for 10/30/2026 to ensure that the waste water leak has been repaired. Ensure that plumbing is maintained in good repair to make sure that sewage is properly conveyed to the point of disposal.
findings.citation_text: 5-402.13 Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: REPEAT Inspector observed the soap dispenser at the back handwashing sink (across from the triple sink) to not be working during today’s inspection. The PIC told inspector that they had put in a work order for the repair. Ensure all food handlers are using one of the two hand sinks that are fully supplied and working until the back hand sink is stocked and in working order. A follow up will occur on 10/05/26 to ensure all sinks are fully supplied and are in working order.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed the nozzles of the slushie machine and the internal surface of the coffee maker to be soil. The PIC was made aware. The PIC clean the various food contact surfaces immediately. Ensure that food contact surfaces such as the one mentioned above are monitored, cleaned, and sanitized at a regular frequency.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.comment: The plumbing line under the triple sink in the back was observed leaking. The PIC was made aware. The PIC assured inspectors that the relevant plumbing repairs will be done. Ensure that the plumbing is repaired to be in compliance with the LAW.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: All Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) certificates have expired. Discussed CFPM course and proctoring with person in charge (PIC). The PIC had 2 of the same educational sheet regarding accredited programs from the Sangamon County Department of Public Health from previous inspectors. All facilities serving food are required to have a CFPM on staff and scheduled during all shifts. CFPMs decrease the incidence of a food-borne illnesses, decrease the number of critical violations, and demonstrate proper food safety practices to their staff.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the soap dispenser at the back handwashing sink (across from the triple sink) to not be working during today’s inspection. PIC is waiting on a new dispenser to be delivered. Ensure all food handlers are using one of the two hand sinks that are fully supplied and working until the back hand sink is stocked and in working order. A follow up will occur on 09/08/25 to ensure all sinks are fully supplied and are in working order.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap. [P]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: The paper towel dispenser at the back handwashing sink (across from the triple sink) was not working during today’s inspection. PIC stated a new battery had been ordered for the dispenser and will be delivered soon. Ensure all hand washing sinks are always supplied with warm running water, soap, and paper towels. A follow up is scheduled for 09/08/25 to ensure today’s violation is corrected.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed two sanitizer buckets located at the barista station to be tested at 100 ppm quaternary ammonia. CORRECTED- PIC remade and tested sanitizer buckets to a proper concentration of 200 ppm. Ensure sanitizer buckets are changed (and checked with facility’s test strips) at a frequency to maintain the proper concentration as recommended the manufacturer's label.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: SECOND REPEAT: Inspector observed the caulking between the splashguards and the sink at the donut prep hank sink to be deteriorated. Nonfood contact surfaces should be smooth and easily cleanable to prevent the harborage of mold and other microorganisms. Clean and re-caulk this surface before the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple areas to be soiled with debris:
1) The floor on the North side of the drive through station (under the register).
2) The floor under the triple sink.
Inspector discussed the areas that need cleaning with the PIC. Floors should be cleaned at a frequency to prevent the build up of soil accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
Both PICs food manager certificates have expired since the last routine inspection. Discussed CFM course options (see General Comments for additional information). Ensure sufficient CFMs are on staff and scheduled to cover all shifts of food prep, service, and clean up.
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
Signed employee reporting agreements are not on file for all employees. Ensure employees are educated on the foodborne illness symptoms and diagnoses that would exclude them from work in the kitchen. Keep signed employee health agreements on file.
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD. [C]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
The soap dispenser at the barista handwashing sink was not working during this inspection. PIC stated that the batteries had just been changed and that the dispenser likely needs to be replaced. All other handsinks were supplied with soap. Ensure soap is provided at the barista handwashing sink.
6-301.11: Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap. [Pf]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
The paper towel dispenser at the dish area handsink was not working during this inspection. CORRECTED- PIC changed the batteries in the dispenser, which then functioned properly. Ensure paper towels are always available at all handwashing sinks.
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. [Pf]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: Caulking observed to be moldy and deteriorating in 1) at the donut prep handwashing sink where the splash guards are caulked to the sink; and 2) where the 3 compartment sink is caulked to the wall. Clean and recaulk these areas.
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris. [C]

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
Several lights are burnt out in the back area. The same bulbs were replaced after the last routine inspection and have burnt out again. Replace burnt out lightbulbs to provide adequate light in the back room.
6-303.11: The light intensity shall be at least a certain lux and present in certain areas. [C]

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: Food handler certificates are not available or are expired for several employees working during this inspection. Ensure current food handler certificates are on file for all employees within 30 days of hire.
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  [C]
